00:04-00:06: Strong relative airflow now implied — woman's hair begins streaming noticeably rearward; antenna still straight; jacket fabric still; background parallax continues

00:06-00:08: Hair streams dramatically backward (substantial airflow, equivalent to highway-speed relative wind); whip antenna remains rigidly vertical in every frame; jacket collar/shoulder fabric shows no visible flutter; arms-crossed pose pins much of the jacket
Whip antenna: thin, light, fully exposed element on the hood — the single most wind-sensitive object in frame besides hair
Woman's chambray/cotton jacket: light-to-medium fabric; collar and shoulder area exposed to the same airflow as hair, though torso fabric is constrained by her crossed arms on the window sill
Desert scrub and distant brush: rigid materials; excluded from wind-response comparison per material confound

findings.invariant_violated: physical influence must affect everything it should
findings.description: From ~00:04 onward the woman's hair streams dramatically backward, implying strong relative airflow (moving vehicle or wind). The thin whip antenna on the hood — a light, fully exposed element that should flex rearward under the same airflow — remains perfectly straight and vertical in every frame through 00:08, contradicting the implied cause.

findings.invariant_violated: wind affects all comparably exposed light materials
findings.description: At peak hair streaming (00:06-00:08) the exposed collar and shoulder fabric of her cotton jacket shows no flutter at all, while her hair is blown violently. Partially mitigated by the arms-crossed pose pinning the fabric and the heavier material relative to hair, so flagged as minor with reduced confidence.
